summary: The 2026 LLM landscape is dominated by frontier model families from Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (GPT), and Google (Gemini), with strong open-weight competition from Meta's Llama and DeepSeek. Enterprise adoption is increasingly mediated through cloud aggregators like AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, Snowflake Cortex, and IBM watsonx, which significantly amplify real-world usage beyond direct vendor APIs. Cost-performance ratios have improved dramatically, with open and low-cost models like DeepSeek now delivering near-frontier performance at a fraction of the price.

models.name: GPT-4o
models.popularity_notes: OpenAI models remain the most-called via direct API and are broadly available through Azure OpenAI Service, giving them massive enterprise reach alongside developer defaults.
models.best_for: General-purpose applications requiring multimodal input and broad tool integration

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.5
models.popularity_notes: Anthropic's Claude is a top choice for coding and agentic workflows and is available across AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex, driving heavy enterprise consumption.
models.best_for: Software development, agentic workflows, and enterprise coding assistants

models.name: Gemini 3 Pro
models.popularity_notes: Released November 2025, Gemini 3 Pro (with Deep Think) is deeply integrated into Google Cloud Vertex AI and Workspace, giving it enormous enterprise and developer distribution.
models.best_for: Long-context document analysis and multimodal reasoning at scale

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.popularity_notes: Meta's open-weight Llama leads HuggingFace download stats and is hosted across AWS Bedrock, Azure, Vertex AI, and IBM watsonx, making it the default open model for self-hosted and enterprise deployments.
models.best_for: Self-hosted deployments and cost-sensitive production applications

models.name: GPT-4o mini
models.popularity_notes: As OpenAI's low-cost default for high-volume tasks, GPT-4o mini sees enormous API call volume and is available via Azure OpenAI for enterprise workloads.
models.best_for: High-volume, cost-sensitive tasks like classification and summarization

models.name: DeepSeek V3.2
models.popularity_notes: DeepSeek V3.2 delivers roughly 90% of GPT-5.4's performance at 1/50th the cost, driving rapid adoption among cost-conscious developers and strong HuggingFace download numbers.
models.best_for: Cost-efficient reasoning and large-scale deployments on a budget

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.popularity_notes: Anthropic's fast, low-cost tier is widely used for high-throughput tasks and benefits from the same multi-aggregator availability (Bedrock, Vertex, Cortex) as the larger Claude models.
models.best_for: High-volume, latency-sensitive enterprise tasks requiring Claude quality

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
models.popularity_notes: Gemini Flash's combination of large context and very low cost makes it a high-volume favorite, distributed widely through Vertex AI and Google's developer platforms.
models.best_for: High-volume long-context processing and multimodal pipelines

models.name: DeepSeek R1
models.popularity_notes: A 671B-parameter MoE reasoning specialist (37B active) priced at $0.55/$2.19, R1 is a popular open-weight choice for math and algorithmic reasoning with strong HuggingFace adoption.
models.best_for: Mathematical, scientific, and algorithmic reasoning tasks

models.name: Gemma 2 27B
models.popularity_notes: Google's open-weight Gemma family is widely downloaded on HuggingFace for lightweight self-hosted and on-device use and is accessible via Vertex AI.
